[b]A HACKER GROUP SEARCHING THE TRUTH[/b]
[i]Hacknet[/i] was available for free in Humble Bundle for a short period, long time ago. It's one of those game that normally I wouldn't buy. The game is centered on group of hackers that receives some contracts from people that wants to obtain something: it could be retrieving a file or cancel something from another user computer. For the entire game, you will see the Hacknet OS, a system that allows to execute some tools and let you inside other networks and devices.

[h1]VERY REPETITIVE GAMEPLAY[/h1]
At the beginning [i]Hacknet[/i] seems promising. The game make you feel like you are a real hacker, trying to break in other people computers, but after a while everything repeat itself. You always do the same things: hack devices ports, with specific executables that you just need to download from the hacker group server, once you are in, you need to check the files, and once you completed the task, simply reply to the client request mail, with details needed. Some of these contract are challenging and it will take a lot of time, trying to understand which is the solution of the enigma. Usually there is not only one way to go, but you can complete the mission in different ways. The real problem is that missions are all the same and nothing really change for the whole game.

[h1]CANCEL THE LOGS[/h1]
One of the things that the game never stop to stress you out is deleting the logs in a computer after you finished to snoop around. At the beginning I did it, because I was scared that I could be traced, losing the mission. After a while, because you have so many steps to do in order to complete the contract, I forgot to clean them several times, and nothing happened. They cannot trace me so I simply stopped to worry about it: I canceled only when I remembered.

[h1]CONCLUSION[/h1]
[i]Hacknet[/i] could have potential. It looks different and interesting, but, as I've mentioned before, you need to do always the same bunch of actions, and this made me lose the interest in the game. I have still to complete the main story, but I think I played enough to express an opinion on this title. I really wanted to buy also DLCs, but after this experience, I think I stop here my experience with this game.

I love this game, and I highly recommend it!
(But get it on sale. Discounts always make purchases better, IMO).

This game is different from many other games. Long story short, this game is a hacking simulator, but unlike other hacking games like WATCH_DOGS, this game is completely text based. There are some visual aids, but the game consists of typing codes into a command prompt. It sounds boring, but once you start learning the commands and diving into the story, the game becomes fun really quick. If you aren't interested in hacking at all, then you probably won't like this game. If you have any interest in hacking, this game becomes fun quickly. I got the game for free from Humble Bundle, but I would have purchased the game if I new about it before Humble Bundle.

Besides the DLC, there are dozens of free workshop extensions which are also great!

I feel slightly bad giving this game a negative review given that I enjoyed most of the time I spent playing it, but I honestly can't recommend it.

The positives are more than adequately covered in other reviews, but for completeness: It does a solid job of recreating the Hollywood hacker fantasy, with hacks and counter-hacks, proxies, firewalls, trace countdowns, and all that good stuff. The story is nicely paced, with plenty of humour and knowing pop-culture references as you move from small-time nuisance hacks to big-time corporate takedowns. And there is a mildly satisfying payoff when you figure out the occasional less-than-straightforward mission or discover a new mechanic.

Therein lies one of the major problems for me, though. For the most part the missions are fairly routine and don't really require any genuine creativity or problem-solving. You are pretty much handed the tools you need as you need them, and for each obstacle you need to overcome there will be a single tool for the job. As an example: the procedure for bypassing a firewall is to repeatedly type the 'analyze' command until you get the solution, and then to type in that solution - once you have done that once, it is entirely routine. I rarely felt clever solving the missions, and for a game like this I consider that a major failing.

As another reviewer pointed out, there are also elements of the game that seem to be either completely superficial or just unfinished. The best example is the scrubbing of logs, which is quite laborious, but presented at the beginning of the game as a vital measure to cover your tracks. So, the player diligently does so, until inevitably one time they forget, and then DUN DUN DUN...nothing. Apparently this feature is better implemented in the DLC extensions, but I didn't get that far.

Finally, the aspect of the game that ultimately ruined it for me: it is possible to irrevocably break your save game and have no way to recover. If you accidentally delete a file that is mission-critical to the main storyline, and don't notice until the next auto-save (or you save the game yourself), it's game over. This happened to me at about the 4.5 hour mark, and while it certainly wouldn't have taken me that long to get back to the same point from scratch, the game just doesn't work as a rogue-like - I would be going through exactly the same fiddly steps to complete exactly the same routine missions, and I just couldn't face it.

If you want to play a hacking game with a similar aesthetic but some genuine code-based problem-solving, I'd strongly recommend EXAPUNKS, or for an absolutely brilliant command-prompt-based-rogue-like try Duskers.

[h1] F♥cking awesome...[/h1]
...if you have half a brain and aren't deterred by the idea of sifting through text.

[h1]Become the 'hacker' [/h1]

Hacknet completely immerses you into the role of a stereotypical hacker. Though it is not a perfect game, it shines when a timer is ticking down, intense synth-wave is blaring, red lights are flashing, and you're frantically trying to figure out what the f♥ck is going on.

After a bit of confusion at the start, I guarantee that you'll begin to get the hang of and enjoy the puzzles. The level of detail demonstrated in the files was also interesting, and some of the Bash quotes got some good chuckles out of me. For example, I'm pretty sure I found a list of valid steam keys in one of the files. Used, of course, but the devs really did put some in there, which was cool.
There are some hangups in the gameplay here and there, but overall, it is a phenomenal experience, and it seems like the developers enjoyed making the game about as much as I enjoyed playing it. It is a phenomenal price, too, and this game was also created by a smaller group. Bravo.

I also recommend the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/521840/Hacknet__Labyrinths/] DLC[/url], especially on sale.
